title: Pin firstmate main at study start and test the core calls it
summary: When a study job is dispatched, Athena's core resolves firstmate's main (github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate) to a SHA through a pinner trait, records the SHA in the job record, and mounts the pinned tree read-only inside the agents' working directory. The core's dispatch is tested with a fake pinner, which fixes the finding that sank the earlier attempt.

defaults_applied.how: All new code and tests are Rust.
The core-calls-it dispatch test, the negative change-capability test, and pinner unit tests, with cargo test and clippy clean.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier can run.
Reuse git through the existing athena-git wrapper rather than adding a git crate; record the call.
One focused change: pinner, core call, record field, tests, decision note.
Docs and comments are written for an outside reader.
Read-only is enforced by file permissions and the agent grant, not prose alone.
The firstmate URL is public. Nothing secret or personal is committed.

assumptions: The repository has no pinning code yet. A grep for pinner/pin_instance found nothing, so the earlier attempt's work is not in this copy and is rebuilt.
'Study starts' means the core's dispatch of a job whose reading selects the study capability, not a separate command.
The pin is a firstmate-specific instance setting for the study capability, so the URL and branch live in the study capability's config or a core constant, and the core resolves the SHA.
Pinning uses the git CLI through the existing athena-git wrapper or similar, not a new crate.
The real pinner is not run against GitHub in tests. Tests use local file:// repos and fakes.

Read-only means the checkout's files and directories are chmod'd read-only and the agent grants include no write access to it, within the agents' working directory. A new optional field on Job is acceptable as a record schema change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A pinner abstraction (trait) in athena-core resolves a git remote's main branch to a full 40-hex SHA and checks out that tree, with a real implementation that uses git and a fake for tests. The core owns the call, not an agent.
The firstmate URL https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate and branch main are set in one place (config or a constant), not scattered through the code.

run.rs dispatch calls the pinner only for the study capability, before the prediction commit. The resolved SHA, URL and branch are stored in the Job record (a new optional field), so the SHA is committed before any agent work. The change capability never calls the pinner.

The pinned tree is placed read-only inside the agents' working directory for both the producer and the verifier. File permissions are read-only and the checkout has no write grant. Docs state how this is enforced.

A dispatch-level test builds Athena with a fake pinner that counts calls, and a scripted fake agent driver running the study capability. It asserts the fake pinner was called exactly once, that the Job record carries the fake SHA, and that the mount path exists in the agents' working directory. Run `cargo test -p athena-core` and `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
A second dispatch-level test with the real Change capability and the same counting fake pinner asserts zero pinner calls and no pin in the Job record. Run `cargo test`.

Unit tests cover the real pinner against a local file:// git repository in a temp dir, with no network. They cover resolving main to the expected SHA, an error when the branch is missing, and the read-only mount. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

Removing the pin call in run.rs would fail at least one test. The verifier checks this by reading the tests, and `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.

The decision record (alternatives considered, reversal cost) goes in docs/decisions.md, and the CHANGELOG notes the change. Nothing in the diff includes secrets, personal data or network-dependent tests.

out_of_scope: Studying firstmate or making claims about what it does.
Pinning anything other than firstmate main.
Changes to CI, athena.toml lints, or other governance config, except possibly an athena.toml instance key.
departures: The reference is for a typical job. This change spans the core, a record schema, a mount and dispatch-level tests, and the earlier attempt already failed once, so I forecast cost, time and verification risk worse than the reference.
